newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius business, unions divided over budget.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius business, unions divided over budget.

text.p: A leading private sector organisation on the Indian Ocean Island of Mauritius praised the budget on Tuesday, but unions criticised plans for privatisation and value added tax (VAT).

Finance Minister Vasant Bunwaree said in Monday's 1997/98 budget speech he would propose legislation on VAT in the next financial year to improve revenues and facilitate investment, but gave few details.

He also proposed a $97.2 million fund for socio-economic development, funded by the sale of an as yet undisclosed stake in the government's Overseas Telecommunication Services Ltd. He said he would scrap a levy on the important sugar industry introduced last year.
The budget foresees a drop in the government's deficit to 3.6 percent of gross domestic product in 1997/98 from 4.6 percent on 1996/97.
The Mauritius Joint Economic Council (JEC), which co-ordinates private sector bodies, said the budget would restore private sector confidence sending the right signals to investors.

"The element of confidence between government and the private sector is a vital factor in economic development and any loss of such confidence would only entail negative impact on the economy," said JEC Director Raj Makoond and President Francis Piat in a joint statement.
"The new budget's tone is positive. It's a budget that gives the manufacturing sector the possibility to express itself fully," they added.
But National Trade Union President Rashid Imrith said it was a "bikini budget, hiding the essential".

"With the establishment of a Privatisation Fund, the government has taken the wrong path...The fact that the minister has not revealed the VAT taxation rate scale, we feel that he has a hidden agenda. So we have been trapped, and the consumers too," said Imrith and Mauritius Labour Congress General Secretary Jugdish Lollbeeharry in a joint statement.
They added the budget was incompatible with workers' aspirations.
Bunwaree also announced a series of measures and incentives to boost manufacturing, tourism, training, financial services and sugar industry sectors.
